subject: Helix Thera — TPS headroom & Dedicated capacity proposal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Helix Thera — TPS headroom & Dedicated capacity proposal

Sam / Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on the clinical pipeline and the user flows. Per our conversation, I put together the ask we discussed so engineering can size a dedicated slab and estimate whether a Dedicated commitment meets your SLOs. Attached is a small sample CSV with recent sample payloads (helix_workload_samples.csv). Could you confirm the following so we size correctly?

- Average tokens per request (you mentioned ~450 tokens on average)
- Peak concurrent requests during busiest 15-minute window
- Percent of requests using streaming vs single-shot generation
- Any hard p95 latency SLOs (app-facing) — we heard 250ms target but you mentioned a tighter goal for clinical review flows

What we'll deliver from our side once we have those numbers: a tokens/sec map with recommended GPU count/SKU, latency p95 projections for your primary model (we assumed gpt-neox-20B-quant), and a recommended headroom multiplier for bursts and growth. Our goal is to give you a recommended Dedicated slab (GPU SKU + count), an expected p95 under normal and peak, and an optional hybrid fallback plan (hosted burst) so you don't miss critical windows.

If you prefer, we can do a short technical sync tomorrow with Ben (inference lead) to walk the math.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: helix_workload_samples.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

Alex — thanks. Quick clarifications below and attached is a short ops snapshot (we couldn't export everything cleanly so I pasted the busiest hour):

- Average tokens per request: 420–480 (median ~440)
- Peak concurrent requests (15-min window): ~320 concurrent handlers (this is during lab result spikes)
- Streaming: ~30% of our requests use streaming (real-time status updates for clinicians)
- Desired p95: 200ms for clinical review flows; non-critical background jobs can be 500ms
- Growth: expecting 25% MoM during trial ramp for next 3 months

We'd like to see both a cost-optimized committed slab and a higher-throughput slab for pilot spikes — hopefully with an easy failover path to hosted.

Also looping procurement (procurement@helix-thera.com) for later in the thread.

Thanks,
Sam Tanner

sam.tanner@helix-thera.com

- Model assumption: gpt-neox-20B-quant (we may recommend a different variant if needed)
- Target p95: 200ms (clinical review flows)

Please include: tokens/sec mapping, expected p95 under normal vs peak, recommended Dedicated SKU + count, and a short fallback plan (hosted burst %). Attach an xlsx with the calculation tab.

Sam / Jordan — Ben will share the sizing; happy to set a 30-min tech review after the first draft.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Helix Thera — TPS headroom & Dedicated capacity proposal

Alex / Sam — attached is our initial sizing (capacity_estimates_v1.xlsx) and a short SLO mapping (slo-mapping.md). Summary below — high level first, then the math.

Executive summary:
- Recommended Dedicated slab (cost vs headroom): 6 x H100-80GB (prod slab) + 2 x H100-80GB as hot spare/burst (total 8 GPUs) OR 10 x A100-80GB (if customer prefers A100 SKU parity)
- Baseline throughput (normal traffic): estimated 78k tokens/sec aggregate across slab (assumes optimized kernels and quantized execution path)
- Peak 15-min window (320 concurrent): projected aggregate demand ~140k tokens/sec -> expected p95 = 190–220ms depending on streaming mix
- Recommended headroom: 1.8x (recommended committed capacity should cover 1.8x of baseline to keep p95 < 220ms during expected spikes)
- Fallback: allow up to 30% of surge served by hosted burst (token-burst routing) with automated throttling to protect baseline slab

Key assumptions and notes:
- Model latency per token: ~0.0025–0.0030 ms/token on H100 path for the quantized model (varies with sequence length and KV cache hit-rate)
- Avg tokens per request: 440 (customer-provided) -> tokens/sec mapping derived from concurrent handlers * avg tokens * request rate per second (we used conservative 0.9 req/sec per concurrent handler during spikes)
- Streaming overhead: streaming requests add ~12% more CPU/GPU overhead in our measurements; accounted for in headroom multiplier
- Growth buffer: sizing includes 25% MoM growth over 3 months, applied to baseline before headroom multiplier

Cost & next steps:
- Preliminary pricing for a 12-month Dedicated commitment (with standard enterprise discount) included in the attachment. If Helix prefers shorter commit, we also provided a monthly slab on a premium price.
- Next step: 30-minute technical review (Ben + infra team) to validate assumptions and walk the spreadsheet. After review we can finalize a formal proposal and draft a SOW for procurement.

Sam — confirm whether you want H100 or A100 preference and I will produce a short canary + roll-out plan (traffic split, cache warm-up, model pinning) for the pilot.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Lead, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Attachments: capacity_estimates_v1.xlsx (Excel, 96 KB), slo-mapping.md (Markdown, 6 KB)
